slides.heading:
The Thing That
Follows Water
slides.subtitle: Part One — What the Water Wants
slides.narration: It's always been there. Ancient, and necessary — the reason the rest of life exists.
A hundred windows. A hundred small, warm lives. Behind one of them, an ordinary evening — and no reason to look at the corner.

slides.anchor:
Three feet away,
something is already growing.
slides.narration: Right now, three feet from this table, in the cold corner no one watches, it has already begun. Without malice. Without judgment.
Where it finds moisture, it grows — and eats whatever is there. Dead plants. Of course.
Dead animals. Absolutely. It doesn't choose. It doesn't care what it eats.
Drywall. Also yes. Except in our home, we give it another name. We call it mold. Rot.
But it only follows moisture. Small and slow — not a problem, until it is. Take away the water, and the rest can't happen.

slides.heading: 48 HOURS
slides.sub: From the moment water arrives to the moment a damp spot becomes a colony.
slides.narration: From the moment water arrives, you have roughly forty-eight hours before a damp spot becomes something alive.

slides.heading:
It was never
the enemy.
slides.sub: It's the reason the forest floor isn't ten feet deep in everything that ever died.
slides.narration: It cleared the remains of the past to make room for what comes next. The cycle of life depends on it. Your building is just a patch of forest floor no one told it was off-limits.

slides.anchor:
Most days, nothing.
That's the bet paying off.
slides.narration: So you check the places water hides. A dry pan. A dry corner. Most days, nothing — and that is not wasted time. That is the bet paying off.

slides.heading:
Control the moisture,
control the mold.
slides.sub: You can't out-clean it. You can own the one thing it needs.
slides.narration: You can't out-clean it. But you can own the one thing it needs. Control the moisture. Prevent the rot.
One building. A hundred doors. Behind them, the four small habits that catch the water before it ever reaches a wall like the one you just saw.

quiz.question: Fundamentally, the course reframes mold as:
options: A cleaning problem you've fallen behind on
A decomposer that follows moisture and eats whatever is wet
A ventilation issue and nothing more
A cosmetic stain on the surface of a wall

The system working — the check paying off
